clue.text: See 24
Animal spirit of small wooden vessel

parts.note: the pig is the animal
gin is a spirit, the distilled drink

explanation.surface: A boozy farm animal's drink served in a little wooden pail.
explanation.definitionFit: A piggin is a dialect word for a small wooden pail or drinking vessel with one stave as a handle.

clue.text: Dramatic split worth a full apology?

indicators.note: an apology for something is a poor version of it, so the words worth a full come out mangled, rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a dramatic falling-out deserves a complete apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apology' as in 'a poor apology for a meal' signals a botched version of the letters, an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre the imaginary barrier dividing actors from the audience is a split the drama keeps.

clue.text: Container to take animal food

parts.note: a can is a container
an ape is the animal

explanation.surface: Instructions for packing an animal's dinner into a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack served at parties, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Animal clue: odd little thing

parts.note: the mole is the burrowing animal

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of clue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter remarks that an animal clue is a strange small affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule is a tiny particle of matter, about as little a thing as chemistry names.

clue.text: Prompt small audible noise from animal

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: audible tells us to go by the sound of the word purr, written as three letters with the same sound

parts.note: a purr is the contented noise a cat makes

explanation.surface: A quick hint: there is a faint sound coming from the creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audible' means we keep only the sound of purr, spelt PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone is to urge or goad them on, a synonym of prompt as a verb.

clue.text: Slaughter of gnu in den without respite

indicators.note: slaughtering something tears it apart, so the letters of the words gnu in den are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gnu is killed in its lair in a relentless massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never stops goes on endlessly, giving no break or respite at all.

clue.text: Produced from animal earmarked as a potential father

indicators.note: produced from tells us the letters come out of the run animal earmarked, sitting across the two words

explanation.surface: A beast bred from an animal tagged early for breeding as a sire.
explanation.definitionFit: Only one of the sexes can sire offspring, so a man or a buck is a potential father.

clue.text: Social animal's head nibbled a filling form of food

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so this takes the first letter of animal

parts.note: to have nibbled is to have bit at something

indicators.note: filling means the letter a sits inside the other letters
a form of a word is its letters shaped anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sociable creature's head takes a nibble at some sort of stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' turns FOOD into OFDO, and 'a filling' puts A inside it to give OFADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a party, and the British phrase for a party or celebration of some size is this idiom.

clue.text: Clue to father of animal?

parts.note: pa is a word for father; split the answer into ... and it reads as a clue whose solution is those two letters together, pa

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks for a hint pointing to the sire of some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: 'Clue to' says the answer, split as P AND A, is itself a clue, and what it clues is PA, father.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is the black-and-white bear of China, an animal.

clue.text: Animal of rank eating half a horse

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a tier is a rank or row, one level above another

indicators.note: half a means only one of the two letters of the word for horse is used

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A creature of a particular rank devouring part of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: GG is the nursery 'gee-gee' for horse; 'half a' horse is just G, which 'eating' places within TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the large striped big cat of Asia, an animal.

clue.text: It's not normal to make dancing bear caper without money

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so bear is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means the letter for money is taken away

parts.note: to caper is to prance about
P stands for penny or pence, British money

explanation.surface: Getting a bear to dance and cavort for free is a strange thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' gives ABER from BEAR; PRANCE 'without' its P (penny) leaves RANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberrance is a departure from the usual course, something abnormal.

clue.text: Has-been, broken spirit, lamenting

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word has-been are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A washed-up figure, spirit crushed, mourning what is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore this female spirit wails to foretell a death, so a lamenting ghost.

clue.text: Animal with a number of whiskers

parts.note: the bear is the animal
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so a number

explanation.surface: A creature carrying a certain count of bristles.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskers on the chin and cheeks together make facial hair of this kind.

clue.text: Employ uniform — form of cover is covert

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: covert means covered over, so is sits concealed within the other piece

parts.note: a tile is a form of covering for roofs and floors

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to use a uniform, a camouflage cover kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To utilise something is to put it to use, a synonym of employ as a verb.

clue.text: Take wild animal and dine on hot food

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of animal and dine run free and rearrange

explanation.surface: An order to catch a wild beast and feast on a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'Indian' suggesting curry; the term really means cornmeal, so 'hot food' is a playful stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground maize, often cooked as a warm porridge or mush, is this food in old usage.

clue.text: Animal spirit, ultimately wild

parts.note: elan is dash or spirit

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of wild is taken

explanation.surface: An animal's spirit turns out, in the end, to be untamed.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, so an animal.

clue.text: Caracas: not as exotic as an African capital

indicators.note: not tells us the letters of as are left out of the mix
exotic signals strangeness, so the letters of Caracas are rearranged after the removal

explanation.surface: A travel comparison: the Venezuelan capital is less glamorous than one in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and S ('not as') from CARACAS and rearrange ('exotic') the remaining CARAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana, on the West African coast.

clue.text: Animal only just taking off head of chicken

parts.note: the cow is the animal

indicators.note: taking off the head means the word's first letter is removed

parts.note: hardly means only just, barely

explanation.surface: A beast barely manages to chop the head off a hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the bird losing its head; it is the definition, and 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken as an adjective is slang for fearful or lacking courage.

clue.text: A welcome approach?

definitions.meaning: a Latin greeting of hail or welcome
.... is short for avenue, an approach road lined with trees to a house

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting on the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is Latin for hail, and as an abbreviation for avenue names a driveway approach.

clue.text: Animal, one last pair to appear, God willing, on vessel to save them

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: the last pair of a word is its final two letters, here from appear

parts.note: DV is short for Deo volente, Latin for God willing
Noah's ark was the vessel built to save the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: The final two animals come aboard Noah's boat, God willing, to be saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last pair to appear' gives AR, the final two letters of appear.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is a burrowing African mammal that eats ants and termites.

clue.text: Teaching of animal by its parent

parts.note: the dog is the animal
ma is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A young animal is trained by its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a doctrine or teaching laid down as true by an authority.

clue.text: Waddle about with right loafer

indicators.note: about here means turned around and rearranged, so the letters of waddle move

explanation.surface: Waddling around in a comfortable slip-on shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loafer' suggests the shoe; it means an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is an idler, someone who lingers and dallies rather than working.

clue.text: Pressure intensified and produced hail

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
raised means stepped up or intensified, as when stakes are raised

explanation.surface: A weather report: pressure built and a hailstorm followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather; here it is to acclaim, and 'produced hail' means gave acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to acclaim them, so having produced hail is having lauded them.

clue.text: Boatman, cruel to put animal in oven dish

indicators.note: in means the animal is put inside the dish

parts.note: a pie is a dish baked in an oven
the rat is the animal

explanation.surface: The setter Boatman cruelly bakes an animal in a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is this puzzle's setter, so the clue doubles as a joke at his own expense.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer is a cruel seaman who robs ships, a sort of boatman.

clue.text: Way to get food for animals

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
oats are a cereal food

explanation.surface: Directions for finding something to feed the beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoats are small carnivorous mammals of the weasel family.

clue.text: Amusing chap, Don: perhaps he might join AA?

parts.note: a card is a joker or an amusing person
the Don is a river, in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A jokey fellow called Don might be a candidate for Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: AA reads as Alcoholics Anonymous, but here it is the Automobile Association, the British breakdown and motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is the typical member of a motoring club that rescues broken-down vehicles.

clue.text: Failed animal in role of team leader

parts.note: the camel is the animal here
as means in the role of, as in 'acting as captain'

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter of team

explanation.surface: A beast clumsily cast as the captain of a side, and the whole thing flops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team leader' gives just T, the first letter of team.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish at the bottom of a contest is an idiom for having failed in it.

clue.text: Mounted headless horse in horror

indicators.note: a horse in horror is panicked and thrown about, so its letters rearrange
headless means the first letter of horse is removed

explanation.surface: A rider climbs aboard a horse that has lost its head in terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, so it means went up or mounted.

clue.text: Making an animal noise, children hang around

parts.note: to moo is to make the noise a cow makes

explanation.surface: Kids loiter about making farmyard sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is British slang for to loiter or wander about idly.

clue.text: Animal with pronounced whiskers

indicators.note: pronounced means we keep only the sound of the word hair

parts.note: whiskers are hair

explanation.surface: A creature with noticeably prominent whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like 'conspicuous' but is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hare is a fast long-eared mammal like a large rabbit.

clue.text: Animals given quarter in hovel, with hindsight

indicators.note: in means the compass point is put inside
with hindsight means looking back, so the word for hovel is read backwards

parts.note: a slum is a squalid dwelling, a hovel
E, east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Beasts allowed lodging in a shack, in retrospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With hindsight' turns SLUM into MULS, and E goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are hybrid animals bred from a donkey and a horse.

clue.text: Misguided terror legislation introduced — it maintains an open wound

indicators.note: introduced means the act is put inside the other letters
misguided means led astray, so the letters of terror are rearranged

parts.note: an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: Wrong-headed anti-terror law brought in keeps a wound unhealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misguided' rearranges the letters to RETROR before 'introduced' sets the act in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a surgical instrument that holds back the edges of an incision.
